products.candidate: Single exon 55 skip (54|56 junction) — brief's stated goal, mechanism 'not applicable'
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found as a benign allele. Single-exon out-of-frame deletions in the distal rod are DMD-type; no asymptomatic carrier of an exon-55-only deletion was found in the mild-deletion review (Fortunato 2023) or in BMD natural-history cohorts. Searches: 'exon 55 deletion DMD phenotype', 'mild dystrophinopathy deletion clusters', BMD natural history 225 patients.
products.domain_consequence: Enumeration: exon 55 = 190 bp, frame remainder 1, so the 54|56 junction is out of frame. Product is not an internally deleted protein at all — translation frameshifts just after aa ~2675 (within spectrin repeat 21, UniProt 2580-2686) and stops downstream, losing repeats 22-24, WW (3055-3088), ZZ (3308-3364), the dystroglycan-binding cysteine-rich region and the syntrophin-binding C-terminus (3466-3518).
products.rescue_evidence: None found, and none possible in principle: a frameshifted transcript is itself an NMD substrate. No paper was found reporting dystrophin rescue by exon-55-only skipping.
products.why: Frame arithmetic from the enumeration is decisive — the product is a rod-domain truncate with no sarcolemmal anchor, not a Becker protein.

findings.claim: Dystrophin spectrin repeat 21 spans aa 2580-2686 and repeat 22 aa 2689-2802; WW 3055-3088, ZZ 3308-3364, syntrophin-binding 3466-3518.
Mild/asymptomatic in-frame DMD deletion clusters are 45-55, 48-51, 50-51 and 51-52; no exon-55-only benign allele is listed.

products.candidate: Double skip exons 54-55 (2 exons, 345 bp, Δaa 2625-2739, -115; junction ACAGAAACCAAG|GACCTCCAAGGT)
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found. No reported human del54-55 genomic deletion with phenotype was retrieved. Searches run: 'deletion of exons 54-55 Becker patient' (extended), '"exon 54" "exon 55" DMD deletion in-frame cohort' (extended), Fortunato mild-deletion review, BMD natural-history cohort, Europe PMC (503 error, retried). Closest human anchors are deletions that end at exon 55: del48-55 (asymptomatic 35-year-old male, normal CK) and del45-55 (asymptomatic to mild BMD).
products.domain_consequence: Δ2625-2739 removes the C-terminal ~62 aa of spectrin repeat 21 (2580-2686) and the N-terminal 51 aa of repeat 22 (2689-2802). The junction fuses R21 aa 2580-2624 (45 aa) to R22 aa 2740-2802 (63 aa) = 108 aa, i.e. the length of one canonical repeat (R21 = 107 aa, R22 = 114 aa) — the structurally favourable 'hybrid repeat' configuration rather than a fractional repeat. Everything else is untouched: actin-binding CH1/CH2 (15-240), nNOSμ-binding repeats 16-17 (1992-2208), hinge 3, repeats 23-24, WW, ZZ, cysteine-rich and C-terminal syntrophin/dystrobrevin region. Deletion stays entirely upstream of exon 56, the boundary beyond which no asymptomatic in-frame deletion has been observed.
products.rescue_evidence: No direct del54-55 rescue data found. Indirect: PMO cocktails covering exons 45-55 (which include exon-54 and exon-55 oligos) skip multiple exons and restore dystrophin in DMD patient-derived myotubes; and multi-exon 45-55 skipping cocktails work systemically in mdx52 mice. Exon-54 and exon-55 skipping efficiencies in that work are tool-predicted (62.0% and 120.4%), not measured for a 54+55-only pair.
products.why: Smallest in-frame product, loses only ~1 repeat's worth of distal rod, keeps nNOS-binding repeats and the whole exon 56-79 region, and the junction length predicts a foldable hybrid repeat — but the human genotype evidence is indirect.

findings.claim: Spectrin repeat 21 = aa 2580-2686, repeat 22 = aa 2689-2802 in dystrophin isoform 1 (3685 aa).
In-frame deletions modelled as retaining a hybrid repeat (Δ45-48, Δ45-51) behaved better clinically than those producing a fractional repeat (Δ45-47, Δ45-49), with DCM onset delayed 11-14 years.
In the mild-dystrophinopathy review all asymptomatic deleted intervals lay within exons 2-55, with no downstream exons involved (apart from one exon-78 case).

PMO cocktails skipping exons within 45-55 (3, 8 or 10 exons removed) restored dystrophin in immortalised/transdifferentiated DMD patient cells; predicted per-exon efficiencies included exon 54 = 62.0%, exon 55 = 120.4%.
A cocktail of ASOs skipping exons 45-55 was delivered systemically and evaluated in vivo in mdx52 mice.

products.candidate: Double skip exons 55-56 (2 exons, 363 bp, Δaa 2676-2796, -121; junction CATTCATAAAAG|GTCCCATTTGGA)
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found. Searches: '"exon 55-56" in-frame deletion phenotype Becker' (extended), Fortunato review, BMD natural-history cohort. Relevant negative evidence: no asymptomatic in-frame deletion in the mild-deletion review extended beyond exon 55, and the authors argue the exon 56-79 territory is the functionally conserved core.
products.domain_consequence: Δ2676-2796 clips only the last 11 aa of repeat 21 but removes 108 of the 114 aa of repeat 22, leaving a 6-aa R22 stub; the fused element is ~102 aa, short of a canonical repeat — a fractional/frayed junction rather than a clean hybrid repeat. Repeats 23-24, CR and C-terminus intact; nNOS-binding R16-17 intact. Crosses the exon-55/56 boundary.
products.rescue_evidence: None found specific to del55-56. Exon-56 ASO skipping efficiency was not retrieved in any dataset (the 45-55 cocktail work stops at exon 55), so this block has no oligo precedent at all for one of its two exons.
products.why: Equal on frame and nearly equal on size, but it eats a whole repeat without an equal-length replacement and is the only two-exon option that breaches the exon-56 boundary where human benign deletions stop.

findings.claim: Repeat 22 spans aa 2689-2802, so Δ2676-2796 deletes essentially the entire repeat and leaves a 6-residue remnant.
Asymptomatic deleted intervals were confined to exons 2-55; the 56-79 region is argued to correspond to the ancestral, function-critical striated-muscle part of the gene.

products.candidate: Four-exon skip 52-55 (675 bp, Δaa 2515-2739, -225; junction ATCAAGCAGAAG|GACCTCCAAGGT)
products.natural_human_equivalent: No individually phenotyped human del52-55 case retrieved, but it sits in the exon 45-55 hotspot whose deletions are the classic mild/BMD cluster, and the equivalent mouse allele was made deliberately as a BMD model. Searches: 'deletion exons 52-55 Becker patient' (extended), Fortunato review, MLPA genotype-phenotype cohort.
products.domain_consequence: Δ2515-2739 removes the C-terminal 63 aa of repeat 20 (2475-2577), all of repeat 21, and the N-terminal half of repeat 22. Junction fuses R20 aa 2475-2514 (40 aa) to R22 aa 2740-2802 (63 aa) = 103 aa, close to one repeat length (near-hybrid). Hinge 3 (between R19 and R20, ~2424-2474), nNOS-binding R16-17, CH1/CH2, R23-R24, WW, ZZ, cysteine-rich and C-terminus all preserved; stops at the exon-55 boundary.
products.rescue_evidence: Strongest animal evidence of any candidate here: a CRISPR Dmd Δ52-55 mouse expresses WT-like levels of truncated dystrophin with normal DGC localisation at the sarcolemma, normal grip strength, <1% central nuclei, no fibrosis and no Evans-blue uptake after exercise at 12 weeks; by 52 weeks exercised mice show reduced grip strength and lower contractile force at 75-125 Hz, with cardiac structure/function largely preserved through 52 weeks. No ASO-induced 52-55 skipping dataset found; exon 52 and 53 PMOs exist within the 45-55 cocktails.
products.why: This is the only candidate product with a purpose-built in vivo model showing full-level, correctly localised protein and near-normal muscle, with only a late exercise-stress decrement.

findings.claim: Dmd Δ52-55 mice show WT-like levels of truncated dystrophin with normal DGC localisation to the sarcolemma and normal muscle histology/function at 12 weeks.
At 52 weeks exercised Δ52-55 mice show reduced forelimb grip strength and reduced contractile force at 75, 100 and 125 Hz versus wildtype; cardiac structure and function remain mostly normal.
Spectrin repeat 20 = aa 2475-2577, so the 52-55 junction joins a 40-aa R20 segment to a 63-aa R22 segment.

products.candidate: Four-exon skip 54-57 (675 bp, Δaa 2625-2849, -225; junction ACAGAAACCAAG|GCCTTCAAGAGG)
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found; no benign human deletion extending past exon 55 was identified in the mild-deletion review (only an exon-78 outlier). Searches as above plus 'deletion exons 54-57 DMD'.
products.domain_consequence: Δ2625-2849 removes the C-terminal half of repeat 21, all of repeat 22 and the N-terminal 42 aa of repeat 23 (2808-2930); the fused element is R21 aa 2580-2624 (45 aa) + R23 aa 2850-2930 (81 aa) = 126 aa, oversized relative to a canonical repeat. CR/C-terminal domains and nNOS-binding repeats intact.
products.rescue_evidence: None found for this block; no exon-56 or exon-57 ASO efficiency data retrieved.
products.why: Frame-legal and domain-sparing on paper, but it deletes 225 aa including two exons of the exon 56-79 region where no human benign deletion exists, for no size advantage over 52-55.

findings.claim: Spectrin repeat 23 spans aa 2808-2930, so Δ2625-2849 truncates its N-terminal 42 residues.
Benign/asymptomatic in-frame deletions were confined to exons 2-55 in a 81-patient literature review.

products.candidate: Six-exon skip 50-55 (1017 bp, Δaa 2401-2739, -339; junction CAGCCAGTGAAG|GACCTCCAAGGT)
products.natural_human_equivalent: No isolated del50-55 case retrieved, but it is a sub-interval of the del45-55 and del48-55 alleles that are documented asymptomatic/mild, and it removes hinge 3 exactly as those do. Searches: 'deletion exons 50-55 Becker phenotype' (extended), Fortunato review.
products.domain_consequence: Δ2401-2739 removes the C-terminal 23 aa of repeat 19 (2319-2423), the entire inter-repeat/hinge-3 linker (~2424-2474), all of repeat 20, all of repeat 21 and the N-half of repeat 22; junction fuses R19 aa 2319-2400 (82 aa) to R22 aa 2740-2802 (63 aa) = 145 aa, an oversized non-canonical element. nNOS-binding R16-17 (1992-2208), actin-binding CH domains, R23-24, CR and C-terminus preserved.
products.rescue_evidence: No del50-55-specific rescue found. Indirect: hinge-3-removing rod deletions are the latest-onset cardiomyopathy group in BMD (mid-40s versus mid-20s for N-terminal deletions), and exon-50 PMOs are part of validated 45-55 cocktails.
products.why: Human-anchored by containment within the benign 45-55/48-55 intervals and by the late-cardiomyopathy signature of hinge-3 rod deletions, but it costs up to 6 oligos and gives an awkward 145-aa junction element.

findings.claim: BMD deletions removing part of the rod domain plus hinge 3 are associated with late-onset dilated cardiomyopathy (mid-40s), versus mid-20s for amino-terminal deletions.
Repeat 19 = aa 2319-2423 and repeat 20 begins at 2475, placing hinge 3 within the Δ2401-2739 interval.

products.natural_human_equivalent: None found; extends two exons past the exon-55 boundary beyond which no asymptomatic deletion was observed.
products.domain_consequence: Removes R20 C-half, all R21, all R22 and the N-terminal 42 aa of R23; junction fuses 40 aa of R20 to 81 aa of R23 = 121 aa. CR/C-terminus and nNOS-binding repeats intact.
products.why: Strictly worse than 52-55 — same upstream breakpoint, 110 more residues deleted, and it enters the exon 56-79 region.

findings.claim: No asymptomatic in-frame deletion in the reviewed mild-dystrophinopathy cohort extended beyond exon 55.

products.candidate: Six-exon skip 53-58 (1008 bp, Δaa 2554-2889, -336) and seven/eight-exon skip 54-59 (Δaa 2625-2979, -355)
products.natural_human_equivalent: None found for either; both breach exon 56 and reach exons 58-59.
products.domain_consequence: 53-58: removes the C-terminal 24 aa of R20, all R21-R22 and most of R23, fusing R20 aa 2475-2553 (79 aa) to R23 aa 2890-2930 (41 aa) = 120 aa. 54-59: removes R21 C-half, all R22, all R23 and the N-terminal 45 aa of R24 (2935-3040), fusing 45 aa of R21 to R24 aa 2980-3040 (61 aa) = 106 aa, i.e. hybrid-length but at the cost of ~3 repeats and the loss of most of the distal rod immediately preceding WW/CR.
products.why: They delete three of the four repeats that sit immediately upstream of the WW/cysteine-rich anchor and lie wholly inside the exon 56-79 interval that human genetics flags as intolerant.

findings.claim: Repeat 24 spans aa 2935-3040 and the WW domain begins at 3055, so Δ2625-2979 leaves only a 75-aa stub of rod before the WW/CR module.
Mild/asymptomatic deletion intervals in the literature review stopped at exon 55; the 56-79 region is argued to be the function-critical core.

products.candidate: Eight-exon skip 48-55 (1305 bp, Δaa 2305-2739, -435; junction CAGTGGATAAAG|GACCTCCAAGGT)
products.natural_human_equivalent: Best single human anchor in the whole set: a 35-year-old male carrying a DMD exons 48-55 deletion was completely asymptomatic — normal muscle strength, no pseudohypertrophy, normal serum CK at 198 IU/L (ref 20-270) — found incidentally during prenatal testing of his daughter. Caveat: a single case at 35 years, with the authors noting follow-up is needed.
products.domain_consequence: Δ2305-2739 removes the C-terminal ~14 aa of repeat 18 (2211-2318), all of repeat 19, hinge 3, all of repeat 20, all of repeat 21 and the N-half of repeat 22; the junction fuses R18 aa 2211-2304 (94 aa) to R22 aa 2740-2802 (63 aa) = 157 aa. Critically it stops short of repeats 16-17 (1992-2208), which carry the nNOSμ-binding site, so unlike del45-55 the nNOS site is retained; CH1/CH2, R23-24, WW, ZZ, CR and C-terminus intact.
products.rescue_evidence: No ASO-induced 48-55 skipping dataset found. Exon-48 through exon-55 PMOs individually exist within published 45-55 cocktails, which restored dystrophin in DMD patient-derived myotubes.
products.why: It is the only product in this set with a documented, genuinely asymptomatic adult human carrier, and it keeps the nNOS-binding repeats that del45-55 loses — the problem is purely buildability (up to 8 oligos).

findings.claim: A 35-year-old male with a DMD exons 48-55 deletion was asymptomatic with normal muscle strength and normal CK (198 IU/L), detected incidentally at prenatal diagnosis.
nNOSμ binds spectrin-like repeats 16 and 17 of dystrophin, encoded by exons 42-45.
Repeat 18 spans aa 2211-2318, so Δ2305-2739 clips only its last ~14 residues and leaves repeats 16-17 intact.

products.candidate: Eleven-exon skip 45-55 (the published multi-exon hotspot block; in-frame per literature — exact aa range not in the supplied enumeration, which lists only the 16 smallest of 31 blocks)
products.natural_human_equivalent: The best-characterised human equivalent of any DMD skipping product: del45-55 carriers range from asymptomatic (including a 69-year-old asymptomatic grandfather and two further asymptomatic boys in one family) to mild late-onset BMD; it was the most frequent asymptomatic in-frame deletion (N=6) in the mild-deletion review and the most frequent deletion (17/68) in one cohort; in a 225-patient BMD natural-history study, del45-55 patients did not require ventilation. But phenotype is variable: in 12 biopsied del45-55 BMD patients nNOSμ expression/localisation varied widely and strictly cytosolic nNOSμ tracked with the more severe phenotypes.
products.domain_consequence: Removes the nNOSμ-binding spectrin repeats 16-17 region (aa 1992-2208; nNOS site encoded by exons 42-45) together with R18-R22 proximal sequence and hinge 3. Actin-binding CH1/CH2, R23-R24, WW, ZZ, cysteine-rich and C-terminal syntrophin/dystrobrevin domains intact. This is the one candidate that sacrifices the nNOS site that all the smaller blocks keep.
products.rescue_evidence: The most developed ASO precedent: PMO cocktails (5-6 oligos, mutation-tailored) skip exons 45-55 and restore dystrophin in DMD patient fibroblast-derived myotubes and in immortalised DMD muscle cells; a 45-55 cocktail has been delivered systemically and evaluated in mdx52 mice. No clinical-stage 45-55 cocktail program was found.
products.why: Human genotype-phenotype evidence is unmatched and ASO feasibility is published, but it deletes the most protein, loses nNOS anchoring and needs 5-6 oligos — all unnecessary when the lesion is a single exon-55 PTC.

findings.claim: A family with an in-frame del45-55 included a 69-year-old asymptomatic grandfather and two further asymptomatic boys alongside an affected 5-year-old.
In 12 BMD patients with spontaneous del45-55, nNOSμ expression/localisation varied widely and strictly cytosolic mislocalisation was associated with more severe phenotype.
In a 225-patient BMD natural-history cohort, patients with exon 45-47 and exon 45-55 deletions did not require ventilator use.
Mutation-tailored PMO cocktails of 5-6 oligos induced exons 45-55 skipping and dystrophin restoration in DMD patient-derived myotubes.

products.candidate: Non-skipping mechanisms whose product is a truncated/altered protein: NMD evasion (stabilising the exon-55 PTC transcript), 5'UTR/3'UTR or transcriptional upregulation, and intra-exonic cryptic-site partial exon 55 removal
products.natural_human_equivalent: For NMD evasion/upregulation the product equals the natural rod-domain truncate seen in DMD nonsense patients — uniformly severe DMD, not Becker; no benign human equivalent found. For partial-exon-55 removal, no human allele with an intra-exon-55 internal deletion was retrieved.
products.domain_consequence: NMD evasion/upregulation: protein stops within repeat 21 (2580-2686), losing repeats 22-24, WW (3055-3088), ZZ (3308-3364), the β-dystroglycan-binding cysteine-rich region and the syntrophin-binding C-terminus (3466-3518) — no DGC anchoring. Cryptic-site partial exon 55 removal: would delete an unknown sub-segment of repeat 21/22; therapeutic only if the retained fragment keeps the frame, which is unverified.
products.rescue_evidence: None found. No ASO-mediated readthrough or NMD-evasion rescue of a DMD nonsense allele producing functional dystrophin was retrieved; readthrough is a small-molecule mechanism, not an oligo one.
products.why: More of a protein that cannot bind β-dystroglycan is not therapy, and the cryptic-site route depends on a site nobody has shown exists at a frame-compatible position.

findings.claim: The β-dystroglycan-anchoring WW/cysteine-rich module (3055-3364) and syntrophin-binding C-terminus (3466-3518) lie far downstream of exon 55 and are absent from any exon-55 PTC truncate.

ranking_rationale: Rank: 54-55 > 52-55 > 48-55 > 50-55 > 45-55 > 55-56 ≈ 54-57 > 52-57 > 53-58/54-59; single exon-55 skip and NMD/upregulation routes are dead. 54-55 is smallest, keeps nNOS repeats and all of exons 56-79, and its 108-aa junction predicts a foldable hybrid repeat; 52-55 adds a BMD mouse showing WT-level, correctly localised dystrophin; 48-55 has the one asymptomatic human carrier.
